events.text: Rumi for a Restless Heart
events.sub: Five Persian Sufi poems with English translation

events.text: Five short poems by Rumi, from the original Persian.
For a restless heart. Stay with each one for a moment.

events.fa: بشنو این نی چون شکایت می‌کند
events.en: Listen to this reed, how it complains,
Ever since they cut me from the reed bed,

events.fa: در نفیرم مرد و زن نالیده‌اند
events.en: men and women have wept at my cry.

events.text: These are the first lines of the Masnavi, Rumi's great poem.
A reed flute is cut from the reed bed where it grew.
Every note it plays is a cry of longing to go back.
Rumi says we are like that reed.
So the restlessness you feel may be a kind of homesickness.

fa: بشنو این نی چون شکایت می‌کند
در نفیرم مرد و زن نالیده‌اند

events.fa: هر کسی کو دور ماند از اصل خویش
events.en: Whoever is left far from their source
seeks again the days of union.

events.text: This comes a few lines later, in the same song of the reed.
Whoever is cut off from their source keeps looking for the way back.
For Rumi, that source is the origin of the soul itself.
So our searching is not a flaw.
It is the soul remembering where it came from.

fa: هر کسی کو دور ماند از اصل خویش

events.fa: ما ز بالاییم و بالا می‌رویم
events.en: We are from above, and above we go.

events.fa: ما ز دریاییم و دریا می‌رویم
events.en: We are from the sea, and to the sea we go.

events.text: Here the image is a drop of water and the ocean.
We came from something vast, and we are returning to it.
Rumi says it without fear. Almost with joy.
In his poetry, going home is not an ending.
It is the drop remembering it was always the sea.

fa: ما ز بالاییم و بالا می‌رویم
ما ز دریاییم و دریا می‌رویم

events.fa: مرده بدم زنده شدم، گریه بدم خنده شدم
events.en: I was dead, I came alive. I was weeping, I became laughter.

events.fa: دولت عشق آمد و من دولت پاینده شدم
events.en: Love's fortune came, and I became fortune that lasts.

events.text: Rumi was already a respected scholar when he met Shams of Tabriz.
And still he says: I was dead.
Look at the last line. He does not say love's fortune came to me.
He says: I became that fortune.
Love did not give him something new to own. It changed who he was.

fa: مرده بدم زنده شدم، گریه بدم خنده شدم
دولت عشق آمد و من دولت پاینده شدم

events.en: I have come to lay down my head,

events.fa: عشق تو را به سر برم
events.en: and to carry your love to the very end.

events.text: This is the opening of one of Rumi's best-loved ghazals.
To lay down one's head means to give oneself completely.
One reading hears it spoken to God. Another, to Shams.
Either way, the restless heart finds rest
only when it stops holding back.

fa: عشق تو را به سر برم

events.text: Thank you for listening.
